description:
About the Position

Lund University invites applications for a post-doctoral fellow position assessing global forest dynamics. The project works on large-scale assessment of forest change, combining remote sensing, forest inventory data and modelling to understand how forests worldwide are responding to climate, management and disturbance.

The fellow will process and analyse satellite and inventory datasets, develop assessment methods, and contribute to international collaborations and publications on global forest dynamics. The position is based in a strong remote-sensing and vegetation-science environment, and the appointment is a salaried postdoctoral contract under Swedish collective agreements.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a PhD in forest science, remote sensing, ecology, geoinformatics or a related field, with demonstrable skills in satellite data processing and quantitative ecology. Programming skills and experience with large geospatial datasets are expected. The working language is English, and the fellow joins an internationally networked research group.

Highlights

  • Global forest change assessment
  • Satellite remote sensing and inventory data fusion
  • Disturbance, management and climate interactions
  • Large-scale geospatial data processing
  • International research collaboration
  • Salaried postdoc under Swedish collective agreement

About Lund University

Lund University, founded in 1666, is one of Sweden's largest and most international universities and a member of the League of European Research Universities. Its faculties cover engineering, science, medicine, economics, humanities, social sciences, law and the performing arts, and the nearby Copenhagen area makes the Oresund region a strong research hub. Doctoral students are salaried employees under Swedish collective agreements, and postdoctoral fellowships are advertised through the university's Varbi recruitment portal. The university ranks among the top 100 research universities worldwide in major rankings.
